uncited: It builds on [HAVS with Dynamic LOD](4110-havs-with-dynamic-lod.md) by providing a reduced representation during interaction and refining the image during idle frames.
The method combines object-space sorting, GPU-based image-space sorting via a k-buffer, and iterative compositing to generate a progressive image.
**K-buffer:** A fixed-size A-buffer implemented using GPU textures.
*   **Batch Size:** The number of internal triangles streamed and rasterized in each iteration.
*   **K-buffer Size:** The fixed capacity of the A-buffer.
*   Clear the off-screen framebuffer and the k-buffer.
*   Identify the boundary triangles of the mesh.
**Stream Geometry:** Select the next batch of internal triangles from the sorted list.
**Rasterization:** Rasterize the batch of internal triangles.
*   Let $F_1$ be the front-most fragment and $F_2$ be the second-front-most fragment.
*   Let $s_1, s_2$ be their scalar values and $d_1, d_2$ be their distances from the viewpoint.
*   Use the 3D pre-integrated table to composite $F_1$ and $F_2$ into the off-screen framebuffer.
*   Discard the front-most fragment ($F_1$) from the k-buffer.
*   Clear the off-screen framebuffer and the k-buffer.
*   Reset the triangle stream to the beginning.
*   **When not to use:** When the user requires immediate full-quality rendering without progressive refinement, or when the dataset is small enough to be rendered conventionally.
The method was developed by S. P. Callahan, L. Bavov, V. Pascucci, and C. T. Silva.
It is based on the Hardware-Assisted Visibility Sorting (HAVS) algorithm [Callahan et al. 2005] and extends it to handle larger datasets through progressive rendering [Callahan et al. 2006].
